commitment_model: For participant i, the conditional mean of the untransformed 12-month distress score is β₀ + βT·treatmentᵢ + βL·low_educationᵢ + βTL·(treatmentᵢ×low_educationᵢ) + γ₂·1(siteᵢ=2) + γ₃·1(siteᵢ=3) + γ₄·1(siteᵢ=4). Treatment is coded 1 for program and 0 for control; low_education is 1 for education category 1 and 0 for categories 2–4; site 1 is the reference. Coefficients are unrestricted and unknown; site effects are fixed across education groups, and treatment effects may differ by education but are common across sites within each education group. Participant outcomes are treated as independent; their conditional distribution is otherwise unspecified, with no known population variance or equal-variance restriction.
commitment_null: βTL = 0: the program-control difference in expected 12-month distress is equal for participants with less than high school education and those with a high school education or more. The null does not require either group’s treatment effect to be zero.
commitment_population: Adults enrolled and randomized in the Pathways to Work evaluation at sites 1–4, comparing baseline education category 1 with categories 2–4. No broader target population was specified.
commitment_outcome: The raw distress_m12 Kessler-6 score, ranging from 0 to 24, with higher values indicating greater distress. The estimand is the difference between education groups in their program-control contrasts in expected score.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None. No analyst-imposed row filter, eligibility rule, or complete-case restriction was applied. The education categories define the effect-modifier groups and do not exclude rows.

commitment_model: Let T be randomized assignment, B=employed_baseline (0 or 1), S the evaluation site (1–4), and Y=earnings_m12. The conditional mean is E[Y|T,B=b,S=s] = α_sb + τ₀T + δ(T×B). Site-by-baseline-employment intercepts α_sb may differ freely; treatment effects are constrained to be common across sites within each baseline-employment group. The estimand is the treatment effect for B=0 minus that for B=1, −δ. Regression coefficients are unknown fixed parameters. No parametric observation distribution, known population variance, common-variance restriction, or explicit cross-observation dependence structure was specified.
commitment_null: H₀: δ=0, equivalently the treatment effect among participants not employed at baseline equals the treatment effect among participants employed at baseline. The null does not require either effect to be zero.
commitment_population: Participants represented by the randomized evaluation at its four sites, with the treatment-effect contrast defined between the baseline-not-employed and baseline-employed groups.
commitment_outcome: Untransformed earnings_m12: earnings in dollars during the previous month, measured 12 months after assignment, including recorded zeros for participants not employed.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None imposed beyond the supplied dataset: no analyst-imposed eligibility rule, filter, subgroup exclusion, or complete-case restriction. Both baseline-employment groups and all supplied site records are included.

commitment_model: Participant-level linear conditional-mean model: E[Y_i | T_i, S_i] = α + δ₂·1(S_i=2) + δ₃·1(S_i=3) + δ₄·1(S_i=4) + τT_i, with site 1 as the reference. The model imposes a common additive treatment-assignment contrast τ across sites, with no treatment-by-site interactions; τ is the site-conditioned difference in mean outcome on the probability scale. No parametric observation or error distribution, common or known population variance, or other fixed population parameter was specified. No cross-participant dependence structure was explicitly specified; the model includes one selected outcome per participant and no site-level or repeated-measures dependence term.
commitment_null: H₀: τ = 0, where τ is the common additive treatment-assignment contrast in the conditional mean; the alternative is τ ≠ 0.
commitment_population: Adults seeking work or better jobs who enrolled in the randomized evaluation at its four sites; no broader population transport target was defined.
commitment_outcome: The untransformed binary debt_collections_m12 indicator: 1 if the participant had a debt in collections during the six months before the 12-month follow-up, and 0 otherwise.
commitment_sample_restrictions: none

commitment_model: For participant i, let Y be the 0/1 debt-collections outcome, T the 0/1 randomized assignment, P the 0/1 baseline parent indicator, and S the site. The selected linear conditional-mean model is E[Y|T,P,S] = α + τT + γP + δ(T×P) + λS + κ(S×P), with site represented by categorical indicators. Thus, treatment effects are constant across sites within each parent group, while baseline means may differ by site and parent status; there are no treatment-by-site or treatment-by-parent-by-site terms. No Bernoulli or other observation distribution is specified, and no equal-variance restriction or known population variance is imposed. Participant observations are treated as independent; no additional cluster dependence is modeled.
commitment_null: δ = 0: the treatment effect on the conditional mean of the 0/1 outcome is equal for participants with and without children under 18 in their household.
commitment_population: Adults enrolled in the four-site randomized evaluation, comparing the intention-to-treat effect among those who lived with at least one child under 18 at baseline with the effect among those who did not.
commitment_outcome: Debt collections at 6 months: the indicator coded 1 if the participant had a debt in collections in the prior 6 months and 0 otherwise, modeled on its original 0/1 scale.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None imposed by the analyst: no subgroup-only filter, eligibility rule beyond the supplied trial design, or complete-case restriction.

commitment_model: For participant i, let Y_i be raw 6-month health, T_i the treatment indicator, L_i=1 when education<=2 and 0 when education>=3, and S_i the site. The selected conditional-mean model is E[Y_i|T_i,L_i,S_i]=alpha_(S_i,L_i)+beta*T_i+delta*(T_i*L_i). It allows a separate intercept for each site-by-education-group cell and restricts each education group's treatment effect to be common across sites: beta for L=0 and beta+delta for L=1. The education cutoff at code 2 and the four site categories are fixed design/model values; alpha, beta, and delta are unknown. Participant errors are treated as independent conditional on these covariates. No parametric observation distribution, known population variance, or restriction on population variances was specified.
commitment_null: H0: delta=0, meaning the conditional treatment effect for education<=2 equals the conditional treatment effect for education>=3. All other model parameters are unrestricted.
commitment_population: Adults enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at its four study sites, with the treatment-effect contrast defined between the two education groups.
commitment_outcome: Raw self-rated health at 6 months (health_m6), on its supplied 1–5 scale; no outcome transformation.
commitment_sample_restrictions: No analyst-imposed row exclusions, eligibility filters, or complete-case restriction. Both education groups are retained: education<=2 (less than high school or high school/GED) and education>=3 (some college or bachelor's degree or higher). This is the model's subgroup coding, not a sample exclusion. Supplied trial eligibility applies.

commitment_model: For the untransformed 12-month financial-security score Y, the fitted linear conditional-mean restriction is E[Y|T,L,S=s] = a_{s,L} + bT + d(T×L), where T=1 denotes assignment to Pathways, L=1 denotes education=1 (less than high school), L=0 denotes education=2, 3, or 4, and s indexes site categories 1–4. Thus site-by-education group intercepts are unrestricted, while the treatment effect is restricted to be constant across sites within each education group. The estimand d is the treatment effect for L=1 minus the treatment effect for L=0. No observation distribution, homoskedasticity restriction, known population variance, or other fixed population parameter was specified; no cross-participant dependence structure was modeled.
commitment_null: H0: d=0; equivalently, the treatment effect on 12-month financial security is equal for participants with less than high school education and participants with at least a high school education.
commitment_population: Participants represented by the randomized Pathways to Work evaluation at its four sites; the target contrast is between those with less than high school education and those with at least a high school education.
commitment_outcome: Financial security index at 12 months, on its original 0–20 scale, with higher values indicating greater financial security.
commitment_sample_restrictions: No rows were excluded. The education groups defining the contrast were education=1 versus education=2, 3, or 4; this was an analysis grouping, not an eligibility restriction.

commitment_model: Participant-level linear regression specification: distress = intercept + one common treatment coefficient + fixed indicators for sites 2, 3, and 4 (site 1 is the reference) + residual, within the selected age subgroup. The estimand is the treatment coefficient in this site-adjusted linear projection; treatment effects are constrained to be common across sites because no treatment-by-site terms were included. Participants are the observational units. No parametric observation distribution, known population variance, homoskedasticity restriction, or explicit dependence structure was specified; site was a fixed control, not a cluster or random effect.
commitment_null: The population treatment coefficient in the specified linear projection equals zero: tau = 0.
commitment_population: Participants represented by the randomized Pathways to Work evaluation at its four study sites who were younger than 35 at random assignment.
commitment_outcome: Raw Kessler-6 psychological distress score measured at six months after random assignment, on its 0–24 scale; higher values indicate greater distress.
commitment_sample_restrictions: Analyst-imposed restriction: age < 35 at random assignment. No other analyst-imposed eligibility filter or complete-case restriction; the supplied design enrolled adults seeking work or better jobs, and the codebook reports all variables observed for every participant.

commitment_model: For participant i, the binary outcome has conditional mean E[Y_i | T_i, L_i, S_i] = α_{S_i,L_i} + τ_H T_i + δ(T_i × L_i). T_i is randomized assignment; L_i=1 for education levels 1–2 and L_i=0 for levels 3–4; S_i denotes the four fixed site categories, 1–4. The model allows separate site-by-education-group intercepts and a treatment effect that may differ by education group, but constrains each group’s treatment effect to be constant across sites. The estimand δ is the treatment effect for education levels 1–2 minus the treatment effect for levels 3–4. Participant observations are treated as independent. The conditional mean is specified on the identity scale; no parametric observation distribution or population variance value or restriction was specified. No other population parameters are treated as known.
commitment_null: H₀: δ = 0, meaning the 12-month treatment effects are equal for education levels 1–2 and levels 3–4.
commitment_population: Participants enrolled and randomized in the four-site Pathways to Work evaluation, comparing effects between participants with education levels 1–2 and those with levels 3–4.
commitment_outcome: Employed at 12 months: the binary indicator equal to 1 if the participant was employed in the survey week and 0 otherwise, modeled without transformation.
commitment_sample_restrictions: No analyst-imposed row exclusion or subgroup-only restriction: both education groups are included. Education is grouped as levels 1–2 versus 3–4 for the interaction. No complete-case exclusion affected the supplied data because the model variables were observed for every participant.

commitment_model: Linear conditional-mean model for the 0/1 outcome: E[Y_i | T_i, A_i, B_i, S_i] = α_{S_i} + γB_i + βT_i + δX_i + θT_iX_i, where X_i = (A_i − 40)/10, A_i is baseline age in years, B_i is baseline employment, T_i is assignment, and S_i is site. The four site-specific intercepts are fixed, unknown parameters; baseline employment enters additively. Treatment effects vary linearly with age and are restricted to be common across sites and baseline-employment values apart from that age interaction. The age centering and scaling constants, 40 years and 10 years, are fixed. The conditional observation distribution and variance are otherwise unspecified; no common or known population variance is assumed. Participant observations are treated as independent, with no cross-participant dependence modeled.
commitment_null: H0: θ = 0, where θ is the change in the treatment effect on 12-month employment probability per 10-year increase in baseline age. This imposes no linear age modification of the treatment effect; it does not impose β = 0.
commitment_population: Participants enrolled in the four evaluation sites, with treatment randomized within site, across the baseline ages represented in the trial.
commitment_outcome: The target population is participants enrolled in the four-site Pathways to Work randomized evaluation, across the baseline ages represented in the trial. The outcome Y is employed_m12, the untransformed 0/1 indicator of employment at 12 months, modeled with a linear conditional mean.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None imposed: no subgroup, age cutoff, or analyst-imposed complete-case filter. All supplied participant rows were included; the codebook states that follow-up outcomes and variables are observed for every participant.

commitment_model: For an adult participant i in the age-under-35 analysis population, the conditional mean of untransformed 12-month earnings is E[Y_i | T_i, S_i, age_i < 35] = α + βT_i + γ₂I(S_i=2) + γ₃I(S_i=3) + γ₄I(S_i=4). Treatment T is coded 0/1; sites 1–4 are fixed conditioning levels, with site 1 as the reference. The model imposes an additive linear conditional mean and a common treatment coefficient β across sites; α and the site coefficients are unknown. No full observation distribution, dependence structure, or population variance restriction was specified.
commitment_null: β = 0: the common site-adjusted treatment effect on mean 12-month earnings among participants younger than 35 is zero.
commitment_population: Adult participants enrolled in the randomized evaluation at sites 1–4 who were younger than 35 at random assignment; no broader target population was specified.
commitment_outcome: Earnings in dollars in the month before the 12-month follow-up, analyzed on its original scale without transformation.
commitment_sample_restrictions: Restrict to participants with age < 35 at random assignment. No other analyst-imposed filter or complete-case restriction.

commitment_model: For participant i, the selected conditional-mean model is E[Y_i | T_i, S_i] = α_{S_i} + βT_i, with site-specific intercepts for the four evaluation sites and one common treatment-assignment coefficient β across sites. No observation distribution, residual variance restriction, or cross-participant dependence structure was specified. No population variance or other population parameter was treated as known; the intercepts and β are free parameters. The model does not specify a treatment effect varying by site.
commitment_null: H₀: β = 0, where β is the common treatment-assignment coefficient in the stated model.
commitment_population: The randomized evaluation population of participants enrolled at its four sites; the target is the site-adjusted common assignment effect for this trial population, not a broader population of all adults seeking work.
commitment_outcome: Y is the untransformed binary training_m12 indicator: enrollment in education or job training in the survey week 12 months after random assignment.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None. No analyst-imposed eligibility rule, subgroup, filter, or complete-case restriction was applied; trial enrollment and randomization eligibility are part of the supplied study design.

commitment_model: For participant i, let T_i be randomized assignment (0/1), N_i = 1 − employed_baseline_i (0/1), and S_i identify one of the four fixed evaluation sites (1–4). The selected model specifies E[Y_i | T_i, N_i, S_i=s] = α_s + β_T T_i + β_N N_i + β_TN(T_i × N_i). Site effects α_s are unrestricted nuisance parameters; treatment effects are common across sites within each baseline-employment group. The estimand is β_TN, the treatment effect among participants not employed at baseline minus the treatment effect among those employed at baseline. No parametric observation distribution, population variance value or restriction, or stochastic dependence structure was specified beyond this conditional-mean model; no population parameters were treated as numerically known.
commitment_null: H₀: β_TN = 0, equivalently, the treatment effect on 6-month distress is equal for participants employed and not employed at baseline.
commitment_population: Participants enrolled in the randomized evaluation at its four sites, with treatment-effect heterogeneity defined by baseline employment status. The model specifies common within-group treatment effects across the four sites.
commitment_outcome: Untransformed Kessler-6 psychological distress score at 6 months (distress_m6), on its 0–24 scale; higher values indicate more distress.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None. No analyst-imposed eligibility rule, subgroup filter, or complete-case restriction; baseline employment is a model moderator, not a sample filter.

commitment_model: For participant i, the conditional mean is E[Y_i | T_i, F_i, S_i=s] = α_s + β_T T_i + β_F F_i + β_TF(T_i F_i), where T is randomized assignment, F is the supplied female indicator, and site s is one of 1–4. Site-specific intercepts are included; treatment effects are constrained to be common across sites within each F group. The estimand β_TF is the difference between the treatment effect for F=1 and the effect for F=0. The conditional mean is linear; no full observation distribution, homoskedasticity restriction, known population variance, assignment probability treated as known, or cross-observation dependence structure was specified. Site categories are fixed conditioning levels; regression coefficients are unknown.
commitment_null: H0: β_TF = 0, meaning the treatment effect on the conditional mean outcome is equal for F=1 and F=0.
commitment_population: Adults enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at its four study sites; the contrast is between the treatment effects for participants coded female=1 and female=0 in this trial population.
commitment_outcome: Untransformed distress_m6: the Kessler-6 psychological distress score measured at six months, ranging from 0 to 24, with higher values indicating greater distress.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None; no analyst-imposed eligibility rule, subgroup filter, or complete-case restriction.

commitment_model: Linear conditional-mean model for the binary outcome on its original scale: E[Y_i | T_i, site_i, employed_baseline_i=0] = α + τ T_i + γ₂I(site_i=2) + γ₃I(site_i=3) + γ₄I(site_i=4), with site 1 as the reference. The treatment effect is constrained to be additive and common across the four sites; site-specific intercepts and the treatment coefficient are free parameters. No parametric observation distribution, variance structure, known population variance, or explicit cross-participant dependence structure was specified.
commitment_null: H₀: τ = 0, where τ is the common conditional mean difference for program assignment versus control in the stated model.
commitment_population: Participants in the randomized evaluation across its four sites who were unemployed at baseline; the estimand concerns assignment to Pathways to Work versus control in this trial population.
commitment_outcome: Debt in collections at 12 months (debt_collections_m12), a binary indicator of any debt in collections in the previous six months, modeled without transformation.
commitment_sample_restrictions: The analyst restricted the analysis to employed_baseline = 0. No site filter or complete-case restriction was imposed. Trial enrollment eligibility and within-site randomization are features of the supplied design, not additional analyst-imposed restrictions.

commitment_model: For participant i in site 1, the conditional mean model is E[health_m12_i | treatment_i, site_i=1] = alpha + tau*treatment_i, with treatment coded 0 or 1. Alpha and tau are unknown; site is conditioned on its fixed value 1. This is an unadjusted two-arm mean contrast, with no other covariates. Participant observations are treated as independent. No parametric observation distribution, homoskedasticity restriction, or known or fixed population variance was assumed.
commitment_null: H0: tau = 0, equivalently, the population mean health_m12 is equal under assignment to treatment and control among site 1 participants.
commitment_population: Participants represented by the randomized evaluation population at site 1; the estimand is the treatment-assignment mean contrast within that site, with no broader transport population specified.
commitment_outcome: health_m12: self-rated health 12 months after assignment, on the original 1-to-5 scale (1 = poor, 5 = excellent), with no transformation.
commitment_sample_restrictions: In addition to the supplied trial's enrollment and design eligibility, restrict to site == 1 and complete observations on treatment and health_m12. No other analyst-imposed filters.

commitment_model: For participant i, the conditional mean of the untransformed binary outcome is linear: E[Y_i | T_i,F_i,S_i] = β0 + βT T_i + βF F_i + βTF(T_i×F_i) + Σ(s=2..4)[γs 1(S_i=s) + δs F_i 1(S_i=s)], where T is treatment assignment, F is the supplied female indicator, and S is site. Site 1 is the reference. Site-specific intercepts may differ by female group; within each female group, the treatment effect is restricted to be the same across sites. No baseline covariates are included. Participants are the independent analysis units; no additional within-site dependence structure is modeled. No parametric observation distribution, known population variance, or common-variance restriction was specified.
commitment_null: H0: βTF = 0; equivalently, the treatment effect on the conditional mean of 12-month employment is equal for F=1 and F=0, conditional on site.
commitment_population: Adults enrolled in the randomized evaluation at its four sites, with the treatment-effect contrast defined between participants coded female=1 and female=0. No broader target population was specified.
commitment_outcome: The 12-month employment indicator, employed_m12, coded 0/1 and used without transformation.
commitment_sample_restrictions: Complete observations on employed_m12, treatment, female, and site; no subgroup-only filter. The supplied packet reports all variables observed for every participant, so this rule excluded no supplied rows. The trial's enrollment and eligibility are design features, not additional analyst-imposed restrictions.

commitment_model: For participants with female=1, the conditional mean of raw 12-month monthly earnings is linear and additive: E[Y_i | T_i, site_i, age_i, parent_i, education_i, household_size_i, employed_baseline_i, earnings_baseline_i, months_unemployed_baseline_i] = α + τT_i + site indicators for sites 2–4 (site 1 reference) + coefficients on age, parent, household size, baseline employment, baseline earnings, and months unemployed at baseline + education indicators for levels 2–4 (level 1 reference). The treatment coefficient τ is a common conditional mean difference across the included covariate values; no treatment interactions were included. No observation distribution, known population variance, variance restriction, or dependence structure was specified. Regression coefficients other than the stated reference coding were not treated as known population parameters.
commitment_null: τ = 0, where τ is the treatment coefficient in the stated conditional-mean model.
commitment_population: Participants identified as female in the randomized evaluation at its four sites; the target is this trial-participant subgroup, not women generally.
commitment_outcome: Monthly earnings in dollars for the month preceding the 12-month follow-up survey, measured as earnings_m12 without transformation.
commitment_sample_restrictions: Restricted to rows with female = 1. No other analyst-imposed eligibility, subgroup, filter, or complete-case restriction.

commitment_model: For participant i, let Y_i be 12-month financial security, T_i treatment assignment (0 or 1), B_i baseline employment (0 or 1), and S_i site. The model specifies E[Y_i | T_i, B_i, S_i=s] = α_{s,b} + βT_i + δ(T_i × B_i), with a separate unknown intercept for each of the four sites and two baseline-employment groups. Treatment effects are assumed common across sites within each baseline-employment group. This is a conditional-mean model: no parametric observation distribution, known population parameter, population variance value, or variance restriction was specified. No additional joint dependence structure was specified.
commitment_null: H₀: δ = 0; equivalently, the treatment effect for participants employed at baseline equals the treatment effect for those not employed at baseline, under the model’s common-within-group-across-sites restriction.
commitment_population: Participants enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at its four sites; the target contrast is treatment-effect heterogeneity between participants employed and not employed at random assignment.
commitment_outcome: The untransformed financial security index at 12 months, measured from 0 to 20, with higher values indicating greater security.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None. All supplied rows were included in the pooled model. Baseline employment defines the modeled interaction, not a row filter; no analyst-imposed eligibility or complete-case restriction was applied.

commitment_model: Let Y_i be the 0/1 debt-collection indicator, T_i program assignment (1=program, 0=control), P_i parenthood (1=lives with a child under 18, 0=otherwise), and S_i site. The model restricts the conditional mean to E[Y_i | T_i, P_i, S_i=s] = α_s + β_T T_i + β_P P_i + β_TP(T_i×P_i). This is a linear-probability mean model: β_TP is the parent-minus-nonparent difference in assignment effects on the outcome probability, constrained to be common across sites. It includes site-specific intercepts for fixed site categories 1–4, with no treatment-by-site terms or other covariates. No separate parametric error distribution, dependence structure, or known or common population variance was specified; no population parameter was fixed to a known numerical value.
commitment_null: H0: β_TP = 0; the program-assignment effect on the 6-month debt-collection probability is equal for parents and nonparents under the specified common-across-sites model.
commitment_population: Adults seeking work or better jobs enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at its four fixed sites; the modeled parenthood difference in assignment effects is common across those sites.
commitment_outcome: Debt collections at 6 months: the supplied binary indicator for having a debt in collections in the prior 6 months, modeled on its original 0/1 scale.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None beyond the trial's own enrollment and design. No analyst-imposed subgroup filter, additional eligibility rule, or complete-case exclusion was applied.

commitment_model: Linear conditional-mean model for the binary outcome Y: E[Y | treatment, site=s] = α_s + τ·treatment, with a separate site intercept for each of the four fixed evaluation sites (site 1 is the reference) and one common additive treatment effect across sites. Site intercepts and τ are unknown. The model specifies only the conditional mean; no additional parametric response distribution, known population variance, homoskedasticity restriction, or cross-participant dependence structure was specified. The 1:1 allocation is a supplied design feature, not an outcome-model parameter.
commitment_null: H0: τ = 0, where τ is the common conditional difference in the probability of food insecurity between assignment groups at a given site; the tested alternative is τ ≠ 0.
commitment_population: Participants enrolled and randomized in the Pathways to Work evaluation across its four sites, in both assignment groups; the analysis targets the full trial population without subgrouping.
commitment_outcome: Untransformed indicator food_insecure_m12: whether the participant's household reported food insecurity in the past 30 days at the 12-month follow-up.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None imposed by the analyst: no additional eligibility rule, subgroup, row filter, or complete-case restriction. Eligibility and enrollment are those of the supplied trial design.

commitment_model: For participant i in the selected subgroup, the conditional mean model is E[Y_i | T_i, S_i] = α + τ T_i + Σ_{s=2}^4 γ_s 1(S_i=s), where Y_i is the 0/1 employment indicator, T_i is assignment (0 or 1), and S_i is site (1–4). This imposes a common additive treatment effect τ across sites, with site-specific intercepts and site 1 as the reference. No parametric observation distribution or common-variance restriction was imposed; participant-level errors were treated as independent, with no clustering or repeated-measures dependence modeled. No population variance or other distributional parameter was treated as known.
commitment_null: τ = 0: the treatment effect on six-month employment is zero for participants in the selected education subgroup, under the common-effect-across-sites model.
commitment_population: Participants enrolled in the four-site evaluation who had a high school diploma or GED (education = 2). The estimand is their common site-adjusted treatment-assignment effect on six-month employment.
commitment_outcome: Employment in the survey week at six months after random assignment, coded 0/1 and analyzed on its original scale.
commitment_sample_restrictions: Analyst-imposed restriction: education = 2. No other filter or complete-case restriction was imposed. The evaluation's enrollment eligibility is part of the supplied study design, not an additional analysis restriction.

commitment_model: For participant i, let Y_i be the untransformed 12-month financial-security index, T_i∈{0,1} denote randomized assignment (0=control, 1=program), B_i∈{0,1} denote baseline employment, and S_i∈{1,2,3,4} denote site. The model specifies E[Y_i | T_i,B_i,S_i=s] = α_{s,b} + τ_b T_i for each b∈{0,1} and site s: site-specific intercepts may differ by baseline-employment group, while each group’s treatment effect is constant across sites. No parametric observation distribution, known population mean or variance, or common-variance restriction was specified. Participant rows were treated as independent; no site-level clustering or repeated-measure dependence structure was modeled.
commitment_null: τ_1 − τ_0 = 0: the treatment effect on 12-month financial security is equal for participants employed and not employed at baseline.

commitment_model: Linear conditional-mean model for participant i: E[Y_i | treatment_i, site_i, female_i=0] = α_{site_i} + τ·treatment_i. Site is categorical with levels 1–4; the site-specific intercepts α_s are unknown coefficients, and the treatment difference τ is constrained to be common across sites. No parametric observation distribution, population variance value or restriction, or cross-observation dependence structure was specified; no population parameters were treated as known.
commitment_null: τ = 0: the common site-adjusted treatment-assignment difference in the conditional mean outcome is zero among participants coded female=0.
commitment_population: Participants in the randomized Pathways to Work evaluation at its four study sites who are coded female=0; the target is limited to this trial subgroup.
commitment_outcome: The financial security index at 12 months, in its original 0–20 scale; higher values indicate greater financial security. No transformation was applied.

commitment_model: For participant i in fixed site s∈{1,2,3,4}, let T_i∈{0,1} denote program assignment and F_i∈{0,1} the supplied female indicator. The conditional mean model is E[Y_i|T_i,F_i,s]=α_{s,F_i}+τT_i+δ(T_iF_i), where Y_i is the untransformed health score. The estimand δ is the treatment-assignment effect for F=1 minus that for F=0; the sex-specific effects are assumed constant across sites. Site-by-female intercepts α_{s,F_i} are fixed unknown parameters. No parametric observation distribution, equal-variance restriction, or known population variance was specified; conditional variances are unrestricted. commitment_model: For participant i in site s ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4}, the specified conditional mean is E[Y_i | T_i, S_i=s] = α_s + τ T_i, where T_i is program assignment, α_s are site-specific intercepts, and τ is a common additive treatment effect across sites. No observation distribution, population variance value or restriction, cross-observation dependence structure, or known population parameter was specified.
commitment_null: H₀: τ = 0, the common site-conditional difference in the mean outcome between program and control assignment is zero.
commitment_population: Participants enrolled in the randomized Pathways to Work evaluation at its four study sites; the effect is conditional on site under the common-effect model.
commitment_outcome: Y is the binary indicator of household food insecurity in the past 30 days, measured at 12 months after random assignment, coded 1 for food insecurity and 0 otherwise; analyzed on its original 0/1 scale.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None. No additional analyst-imposed eligibility rule, subgroup, filter, or complete-case restriction was applied; the supplied design's enrollment and randomization define the study population.

commitment_model: Linear conditional-mean model for the untransformed binary outcome: E[Y|T,F,S] = α + τT + γF + δ(T×F) + site indicators + site×F indicators, where T is assignment, F is the female indicator, and S is site. This allows separate site-specific intercepts by F but restricts each gender group’s treatment effect to be constant across sites; τ is the effect for F=0 and τ+δ for F=1. The estimand δ is the female-minus-F=0 difference in treatment effects. No parametric observation distribution, known population variance, or equal-variance restriction was specified. No joint dependence model was specified; the regression has one observation per participant and does not encode cross-participant dependence. Treatment, female coding (1 versus 0), and the four trial-site categories are fixed predictors; no population variance or other population parameter was treated as known.
commitment_null: H0: δ = 0, equivalently, the treatment effect on the conditional mean of 12-month debt collections is equal for F=1 and F=0.
commitment_population: Adults seeking work or better jobs who were enrolled and randomized in the Pathways to Work trial at its four evaluation sites. The target is the gender-coded difference in assignment effects for this four-site trial population, under the model’s restriction of a common effect across sites within each gender-coded group.
commitment_outcome: The 12-month debt-collections indicator, used as coded without transformation: 1 if the participant had a debt in collections in the prior six months, 0 otherwise.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None. No analyst-imposed eligibility rule, filter, subgroup-only restriction, or complete-case restriction; the female indicator defines model groups and does not exclude observations.

commitment_model: Person-level linear conditional-mean model: E[Y_i | T_i, site_i=s] = α_s + τT_i, where Y_i is the 0/1 outcome and T_i is assignment coded 0/1. This specifies additive site-specific intercepts and one common treatment contrast across the four sites, with no treatment-by-site interaction. No observation distribution, population variance restriction, or cross-person dependence structure was specified. The site intercepts and treatment coefficient are unknown parameters, not known constants.
commitment_null: τ = 0: the common site-conditional treatment contrast in the population mean is zero.
commitment_population: Participants enrolled in the four-site Pathways to Work randomized evaluation; the estimand is their common site-conditional intention-to-treat mean difference.
commitment_outcome: Food insecurity at month 6 (`food_insecure_m6`), modeled as the untransformed 0/1 indicator.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None imposed by the analyst: no subgroup, filter, or complete-case restriction.

commitment_model: For participant i at site s∈{1,2,3,4}, the conditional mean model is E[Y_i|T_i=t,S_i=s]=α_s+τt, where Y is the binary outcome and treatment is coded 0/1. Site-specific intercepts are unrestricted nuisance parameters; the treatment effect τ is constrained to be common across the four sites and is the site-conditional risk difference. commitment_population: Participants randomized in the four-site Pathways to Work evaluation; no population beyond those evaluation sites was specified.

commitment_model: For participant i, the untransformed 12-month distress score has a linear conditional mean: E[Y_i | T_i, site_i] = β₀ + τT_i + γ₂I(site_i=2) + γ₃I(site_i=3) + γ₄I(site_i=4), using site 1 as the reference. The model has one common additive treatment coefficient across sites, with no treatment-by-site interaction. τ is the site-adjusted intention-to-treat effect, averaged over the trial population represented by its site composition. The regression specification does not impose a parametric observation or error distribution, a known population variance, or a dependence structure; no population parameters were treated as known.
commitment_null: H₀: τ = 0, the site-adjusted additive treatment effect on 12-month distress is zero.
commitment_population: Adults enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at its four study sites; the target is the evaluation population represented by those sites.
commitment_outcome: Individual Kessler-6 psychological distress score at 12 months, on its original 0–24 scale; higher scores indicate more distress.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None. All supplied participant rows were included; no analyst-imposed subgroup, filter, or complete-case restriction was applied. Trial eligibility and enrollment are features of the supplied design.

commitment_model: Additive linear conditional-mean model for participant i: E[Y_i | T_i, S_i] = α_{S_i} + τT_i, where S_i is one of sites 1–4, each site has its own intercept, and τ is a common treatment effect across sites. Site is the only conditioning variable; no baseline covariates or treatment-by-site terms were included. No parametric observation distribution, population variance value or restriction, or dependence structure between participants was specified. The site categories are fixed design factors; their intercepts and τ are unknown.
commitment_null: H0: τ = 0, the common site-adjusted population mean difference between assignment groups is zero; the alternative is τ ≠ 0.
commitment_population: Participants enrolled in the randomized evaluation at its four sites; the analysis targets the effect of assignment to Pathways to Work versus control for this trial population. No broader target population was specified.
commitment_outcome: The six-month financial-security index, fin_security_m6, in its original 0–20 point scale, with higher values indicating greater security; no transformation was applied.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None imposed by the analysis: no subgroup, filter, or complete-case exclusion. The supplied trial’s enrollment and randomization define its design population; the supplied observations were complete.

commitment_model: For participant i, the conditional mean is E[Y_i | T_i, E_i, S_i] = α + τT_i + γE_i + δ(T_i × E_i) + λ₂1(S_i=2) + λ₃1(S_i=3) + λ₄1(S_i=4), with site 1 as reference. T is assignment coded 0/1; E is 1 for education levels 3 or 4 (some college or more) and 0 for levels 1 or 2 (high school/GED or less). The estimand δ is the difference between the site-adjusted treatment effects in those two education groups. The model has additive site effects and a common treatment-by-education contrast across sites. No parametric observation distribution, population variance value or restriction, or dependence structure was specified. The regression coefficients, including site effects, are unknown; no population parameters are treated as known.
commitment_null: H₀: δ = 0, meaning the site-adjusted treatment effect on six-month distress is equal in the two education groups.
commitment_population: Adults enrolled and randomized in the Pathways to Work evaluation at sites 1–4. The target is this trial population; no broader population to which results should be transported was specified.
commitment_outcome: Untransformed six-month psychological distress score, distress_m6, on the Kessler-6 scale from 0 to 24; higher scores indicate greater distress.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None beyond the supplied evaluation's eligibility and randomization. Both education groups are included jointly in the interaction model; no subgroup-only, outcome-based, or complete-case filter was imposed.

commitment_model: For participant i, the untransformed binary outcome Y_i = food_insecure_m12 is modeled with an additive linear conditional mean: E[Y_i | T_i, S_i, X_i] = α + τT_i + site indicators + linear terms for age, female, parent, education, household size, employed_baseline, earnings_baseline, and months_unemployed_baseline. Treatment is coded 1 for program assignment and 0 for control; sites are categories 1–4, with site 1 as the reference. The same treatment contrast and covariate slopes apply across sites and covariate values; no interactions were included. The estimand is τ, the common adjusted difference in the probability of 12-month food insecurity by assignment. No parametric observation distribution or cross-participant dependence structure was specified. No population variance restriction or population coefficient was treated as known; the listed covariates and site are conditioning variables.
commitment_null: H0: τ = 0, the common adjusted assignment difference in the probability of 12-month food insecurity is zero.
commitment_population: The randomized evaluation population of enrolled adults seeking work or better jobs at its four study sites; the model targets a common adjusted assignment contrast for this trial population.
commitment_outcome: food_insecure_m12: the original 0/1 indicator for reporting household food insecurity in the past 30 days at the 12-month follow-up; no outcome transformation.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None beyond the supplied evaluation cohort: no analyst-imposed subgroup, filter, or complete-case restriction.

commitment_model: Linear conditional-mean model for binary Y = food_insecure_m12: E[Y | T, B, S=s] = α_s + βT + γB + δ(T×B], where T is assignment (0/1), B is baseline employment (0/1), and s is site. There are additive site-specific intercepts α_s for the four fixed site categories 1–4; β, γ, and δ are common across sites. Thus, treatment and baseline-employment effects have no site interactions, and the treatment-effect difference by baseline employment is δ. No observation-level distribution, population variance value or restriction, or across-observation dependence structure was specified. All coefficients are unknown; no numerical population parameter was treated as known.
commitment_null: H₀: δ = 0; equivalently, the treatment effect on the conditional mean of 12-month food insecurity is equal for participants employed and not employed at baseline.
commitment_population: Adults enrolled in the four-site Pathways to Work randomized evaluation, in either assignment group. The target contrast is the difference in treatment effects between baseline-employment groups, conditional on site under the model’s common-across-sites restriction.
commitment_outcome: The untransformed 0/1 indicator food_insecure_m12, denoting household food insecurity in the past 30 days at 12 months; 1 indicates food insecurity.
commitment_sample_restrictions: none

commitment_model: Participant-level linear conditional-mean model for the raw binary outcome: E[Y_i | T_i=t, S_i=s] = α_s + τt, where treatment assignment t is 0 or 1 and the four fixed conditioning sites s are 1, 2, 3, and 4. The estimand τ is a common site-conditional intention-to-treat risk difference; the model has site-specific intercepts and no treatment-by-site interactions. No parametric observation distribution, conditional-variance restriction, known population variance, or cross-participant dependence structure was specified.
commitment_null: H0: τ = 0, meaning the common site-conditional difference in the probability of employment at 6 months between program assignment and control assignment is zero.
commitment_population: Adults enrolled and randomized in the Pathways to Work evaluation at its four study sites; the target is the common assignment effect for this evaluation population.
commitment_outcome: Employment in the survey week at 6 months (employed_m6), analyzed on its raw 0/1 scale; the estimand is a difference in employment probability.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None; no analyst-imposed subgroup, eligibility filter, or complete-case restriction.

commitment_model: Additive population linear projection of the binary outcome on treatment assignment and site indicators, with a common treatment coefficient across sites: the estimand is the treatment coefficient conditional on the site indicators. No observation distribution, variance restriction, dependence structure, or known population parameter was specified.
commitment_null: The treatment coefficient in that site-adjusted linear projection equals zero: β_treatment = 0.
commitment_population: Adults represented by the participants randomized in the four-site Pathways to Work evaluation; no broader target population was specified.
commitment_outcome: Employed in the survey week 12 months after random assignment, coded 1 if employed and 0 otherwise; no transformation.
commitment_sample_restrictions: none

commitment_model: For participant i, the conditional mean of the untransformed binary outcome Y_i is E[Y_i | T_i, site_i] = α + τT_i + Σ_s γ_s 1(site_i=s), with a common additive treatment effect τ across the four sites and no treatment-by-site interactions. The estimand is τ, the site-adjusted difference in training-enrollment probability between assignment groups. Participants are treated as independent observational units. No parametric outcome or error distribution, common population variance, or known population variance was imposed; conditional variances may differ.
commitment_null: H0: τ = 0, the treatment-assignment coefficient in the stated conditional-mean model is zero.
commitment_population: Participants enrolled in the randomized Pathways to Work evaluation at its four study sites; the target is the trial population, with no extrapolation to people outside it.
commitment_outcome: Training enrollment in the survey week at 6 months after random assignment (training_m6), coded 0 or 1 and modeled without transformation; τ is a difference in probabilities.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None imposed by the analyst. The analysis uses the supplied randomized-evaluation participants without subgroup filters or complete-case exclusions.

commitment_model: For each education level e ∈ {1, 2}, the binary outcome has conditional mean E[Y | treatment, site, education=e] = αₑ + βₑ·treatment + γₑ₂·I(site=2) + γₑ₃·I(site=3) + γₑ₄·I(site=4), with site 1 as the reference. This linear conditional-mean model allows subgroup-specific site baselines and assumes a common treatment effect across sites within each education group; it has no treatment-by-site terms. The estimand is β₂ − β₁. No parametric observation distribution, known population variance, or equality restriction on population variances was specified; the coefficients are unknown. The contrast treats the two subgroup estimates as independent because they use disjoint participants; no other dependence structure was specified.
commitment_null: H₀: β₂ − β₁ = 0, where β₂ is the site-adjusted treatment effect for education level 2 (high-school diploma or GED) and β₁ is the site-adjusted treatment effect for education level 1 (less than high school).
commitment_population: The target comprises adults enrolled in the randomized evaluation at its four sites who are in education level 1 or 2; the estimand compares the program assignment effects in these two education-defined populations.
commitment_outcome: The untransformed binary training_m6 indicator: whether the participant was enrolled in education or job training during the survey week six months after random assignment.
commitment_sample_restrictions: Analyst-imposed restriction: include education levels 1 and 2 and analyze them separately for the contrast; education levels 3 and 4 are excluded. No other analyst-imposed filter or complete-case restriction was applied. The supplied design enrolled adults seeking work or better jobs and randomized participants within site; the codebook reports complete outcome observations.

commitment_model: For participant i, the conditional mean is E[Y_i | T_i, S_i, X_i] = β0 + βT T_i + site fixed effects + γ′X_i, where Y_i is raw earnings_m6, T_i is assignment, and X_i contains age, female, parent, categorical education, household size, employed_baseline, earnings_baseline, and months_unemployed_baseline. The model is additive, with one common treatment coefficient across sites and covariate values and no interactions. Site and education are categorical controls (sites 1–4; education levels 1–4); their coefficients and all other regression coefficients are unknown. No observation distribution, homoskedasticity restriction, population variance, or other nuisance parameter value was specified as known. Participant errors are treated as independent conditional on the included variables; no additional within-site dependence structure was specified.
commitment_null: H0: βT = 0, the treatment-assignment coefficient in the specified conditional-mean model is zero.
commitment_population: The full population represented by adults enrolled and randomized in the four-site Pathways to Work evaluation, with a common conditional treatment effect across sites and baseline covariate values.
commitment_outcome: Earnings in dollars in the month before the 6-month follow-up (earnings_m6), including zero for participants not employed; modeled on its raw scale without transformation.
commitment_sample_restrictions: Complete observations on earnings_m6, treatment, site, age, female, parent, education, household_size, employed_baseline, earnings_baseline, and months_unemployed_baseline. No additional analyst-imposed eligibility filter or subgroup; trial eligibility and enrollment are as defined by the supplied evaluation design.

commitment_model: Participant-level linear probability conditional-mean model for the untransformed binary outcome Y=employed_m6: E[Y|T,B,S]=α_{S,B}+τ₀T+δ(T×B), with zero-mean conditional residuals. T=treatment and B=employed_baseline are coded 0/1; S is categorical site with fixed levels 1–4. The model has an unrestricted intercept for each site-by-baseline-employment stratum, and treatment effects are constant across sites within each baseline-employment stratum. The estimand δ is the treatment effect for B=1 minus the treatment effect for B=0. No Bernoulli or normal observation distribution, common or known population variance, or other population-variance restriction was specified. No joint residual-dependence structure was specified or modeled; site was treated as a fixed conditioning variable, not a random effect.
commitment_null: δ=0: the treatment effect on six-month employment is equal for participants employed and not employed at baseline.
commitment_population: Participants enrolled in the four-site Pathways to Work randomized evaluation, considered in both baseline-employment strata. The model conditions on site and assumes a common treatment effect across sites within each baseline-employment stratum; the target is the trial population, with no extrapolation specified beyond it.
commitment_outcome: Untransformed employed_m6 indicator: 1 if employed in the survey week at six months, 0 otherwise.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None beyond the supplied trial enrollment. Both baseline-employment groups and all supplied participant records were included; no analyst-imposed subgroup filter, site filter, or complete-case restriction was applied.

commitment_model: For participant i, let Y_i be training_m12, T_i be randomized assignment coded 0/1, F_i be the recorded female indicator coded 0/1, and S_i be site. The selected linear conditional-mean model is E[Y_i | T_i,F_i,S_i=s] = α_{s,F_i} + βT_i + δ(T_i×F_i). The site-by-female cell intercepts α_{s,F_i} are unrestricted; the treatment effect is β for F=0 and β+δ for F=1, each constrained to be constant across sites. Y is modeled on its original 0/1 scale. No parametric observation distribution, known population variance, or equality restriction on variances was specified. No additional cross-participant dependence structure was specified. The regression coefficients are unknown; T, F, and site are conditioned-on design variables with the stated coding.
commitment_null: H₀: δ = 0; equivalently, the conditional treatment effect for F=1 equals the conditional treatment effect for F=0, under the model's site-constant effects within each female category.
commitment_population: Participants randomized in the Pathways to Work evaluation at its four sites, with the target contrast between the recorded F=1 and F=0 groups, conditional on site under the specified model.
commitment_outcome: Enrollment in education or job training during the survey week at 12 months (training_m12), a binary outcome analyzed without transformation.
commitment_sample_restrictions: none

commitment_model: Participant-level additive conditional-mean model for the raw score: E[Y_i | treatment_i, site_i, parent_i=0] = α_site_i + τ treatment_i. It has site-specific intercepts for sites 1–4 and a common treatment effect, with no treatment-by-site terms. No observation distribution, residual variance form or fixed variance value, or cross-participant dependence structure was specified; no population variance restriction was imposed.
commitment_null: H0: τ = 0, where τ is the common site-adjusted treatment effect among participants with parent = 0.
commitment_population: The Pathways to Work evaluation population represented by trial participants who did not live with a child under 18 at random assignment, across sites 1–4.
commitment_outcome: fin_security_m6, the raw 0–20 financial security index at 6 months; higher values indicate greater security, with no outcome transformation.
commitment_sample_restrictions: Restrict to parent = 0. No other analyst-imposed eligibility, filtering, or complete-case restriction; the trial’s original eligibility is part of the supplied design.

commitment_model: Conditional-mean linear probability model: E[Y_i | A_i,S_i,B_i] = α + θB_i + βA_i + Σ_{s=2}^4 γ_s·1(S_i=s) + Σ_{s=2}^4 δ_s·A_i·1(S_i=s), where A_i is assignment (0/1), S_i is site (fixed categories 1–4, with site 1 as reference), and B_i is baseline employment (0/1). Treatment effects vary by site; baseline employment enters additively with a common slope and no treatment interaction. The estimand is the site 2 treatment-assignment effect on the conditional mean minus the site 4 effect, δ₂−δ₄. No parametric observation distribution, common-variance restriction, known population variance, or cross-observation dependence structure was specified. No site weights or distribution over sites was treated as known.
commitment_null: H₀: δ₂−δ₄ = 0; equivalently, the site 2 and site 4 treatment-assignment effects on the conditional mean outcome are equal.
commitment_population: Participants seeking work or better jobs who enrolled in the Pathways to Work evaluation at its four fixed study sites. The contrast concerns sites 2 and 4; no population of sites beyond these fixed sites was specified.
commitment_outcome: Six-month survey-week employment, employed_m6: binary 1/0 outcome, with no transformation.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None imposed by the analyst: all supplied rows were used, with no subgroup filter or complete-case exclusion. Trial eligibility comes from the supplied study design.

commitment_model: For participant i in site s and education group g, the conditional mean of the untransformed six-month financial-security score is α(s,g) + β·treatment + δ·(treatment × low_education), where α(s,g) is a separate intercept for each site-by-education-group combination. low_education equals 1 for education=1 and 0 for education=2, 3, or 4. Treatment effects may differ between these two groups but are constant across sites within each group. Errors are treated as independent across participants; no parametric observation distribution, known population variance, or homoskedasticity restriction was specified. No regression coefficient or variance parameter was treated as known.
commitment_null: δ = 0: the treatment effect on six-month financial security for participants with education=1 equals the treatment effect for participants with education=2, 3, or 4.
commitment_population: The target is the enrolled randomized-trial population across its four sites, with the treatment-effect contrast between participants with education=1 and those with education=2, 3, or 4. No broader external target population was specified.
commitment_outcome: Financial security at six months, on its original 0–20 scale; higher values indicate greater security.
commitment_sample_restrictions: No analyst-imposed row exclusions or complete-case restriction; all supplied records had the model variables observed. Both education groups were included, defined as education=1 versus education=2, 3, or 4. This subgroup definition is an analysis choice, distinct from the trial's enrollment eligibility.

commitment_model: For binary Y_i = debt_collections_m12, let T_i be assignment (1 program, 0 control), L_i = 1 for education levels 1–2 and 0 for levels 3–4, and S_i be site. The selected conditional-mean model is E[Y_i | T_i, L_i, S_i=s] = α_{s,L_i} + τ_H T_i + δ(T_i × L_i), for s ∈ {1,2,3,4}. It has a separate intercept for each site-by-education cell and a treatment effect common across sites within each education group; it includes no other covariates or treatment-by-site terms. The estimand δ is the treatment effect below college minus the treatment effect with some college or more, on the untransformed 0/1 outcome scale. No parametric observation distribution, population variance value, variance-equality restriction, or cross-observation dependence structure was specified; no population parameters were treated as known.
commitment_null: H₀: δ = 0; equivalently, the treatment effects on 12-month debt collections are equal for education levels 1–2 and levels 3–4.
commitment_population: Participants enrolled in the four-site randomized evaluation, with the contrast defined between the education groups specified in the model. No population beyond the evaluation participants was specified.
commitment_outcome: Debt in collections during the six months before the 12-month follow-up, recorded as the binary variable debt_collections_m12 (0/1), without transformation.
commitment_sample_restrictions: No analyst-imposed row exclusions, site filters, or complete-case restrictions. Both treatment arms and all four sites are included. The model partitions participants into education levels 1–2 versus 3–4; both groups contribute to the contrast.

commitment_model: Conditional mean model for participant i: E[hours_m12_i | treatment_i, parent_i, site_i] = α + β_T treatment_i + β_P parent_i + β_TP treatment_i×parent_i + site fixed effects for sites 2–4 + parent-by-site interactions for sites 2–4. Treatment is coded 0=control, 1=program; parent is coded 0=no child under 18 at home, 1=child under 18 at home; site categories are 1–4. The model allows treatment effects to differ by parent status but restricts each parent-specific treatment effect to be common across sites. Regression coefficients are unknown population parameters. No observation distribution, population variance restriction, or cross-participant dependence structure was specified.
commitment_null: β_TP = 0: the program’s effect on month-12 weekly hours is equal for participants with and without a child under 18 at home.
commitment_population: Adults enrolled in the randomized evaluation at its four sites, considered within the two baseline groups defined by whether they lived with a child under 18; the target parameter is the difference between those groups’ program effects on month-12 weekly hours.
commitment_outcome: Usual weekly hours worked at month 12, hours_m12, on its recorded scale; the codebook defines this outcome as zero for participants not employed.
commitment_sample_restrictions: Complete cases on hours_m12, treatment, parent, and site. No other analyst-imposed eligibility rule, subgroup restriction, or filter.

commitment_model: For each participant i, let Y_i be distress_m12, T_i the randomized treatment indicator, D_i = months_unemployed_baseline/12, and S_i the site. The selected conditional-mean model is E[Y_i | T_i, D_i, S_i] = α + βT_i + γ(D_i − c) + δT_i(D_i − c) + λ₂1(S_i=2) + λ₃1(S_i=3) + λ₄1(S_i=4), with site 1 as the reference and c the analysis-sample mean of D in the restricted sample. The estimand δ is the linear change, per additional year since the last job, in the treatment effect on distress, conditional on site. Errors are treated as independent across participants and have conditional mean zero; their conditional variances are unrestricted. No parametric observation distribution, known population variance, or homoskedasticity restriction was specified. No population parameters were treated as known.
commitment_null: H₀: δ = 0, meaning the treatment effect on 12-month distress does not vary linearly with baseline unemployment duration among the analyzed population; the alternative is δ ≠ 0.
commitment_population: The enrolled Pathways to Work randomized-trial participants at its four evaluation sites who were unemployed at random assignment. The target is this trial population, not a broader workforce population.
commitment_outcome: The untransformed Kessler-6 psychological distress score at 12 months, ranging from 0 to 24, with higher values indicating greater distress.
commitment_sample_restrictions: In addition to the trial's supplied enrollment and randomization design, the analysis restricted participants to months_unemployed_baseline > 0, which excludes those employed at assignment according to the codebook. No other analyst-imposed eligibility, subgroup, or complete-case restriction was applied.

commitment_model: For participants with parent=1, the conditional mean of earnings_m6 is E[Y_i | treatment_i, site_i] = α_site_i + τ treatment_i. The treatment contrast τ is additive and common across sites; site is conditioned on using fixed effects for sites 1–4. No parametric observation distribution, cross-participant dependence structure, known population variance, or restriction on population variances was specified. No population nuisance parameters were treated as known.
commitment_null: H0: τ = 0, meaning the common site-conditional mean difference in 6-month earnings by treatment assignment among parents is zero.
commitment_population: Participants enrolled in the randomized evaluation at its four sites who live with at least one child under age 18; the target contrast is conditional on site within this evaluation population.
commitment_outcome: Individual earnings in dollars for the month before the 6-month follow-up (earnings_m6), on the recorded, untransformed scale.
commitment_sample_restrictions: Analyst-imposed restriction: retain parent=1 only. No other analyst-imposed filter or complete-case restriction. Trial enrollment and survey completion are features of the supplied evaluation design.

commitment_model: For participants with employed_baseline = 0, the model is the additive linear conditional mean E[Y_i | T_i, S_i] = α + τT_i + γ₂·1(S_i=2) + γ₃·1(S_i=3) + γ₄·1(S_i=4), with site 1 as reference. Treatment is coded 0/1, and τ is a common treatment effect across the four sites; there are no treatment-by-site terms. The intercept, treatment effect, and site effects are unknown. No parametric observation distribution, population variance value or restriction, or explicit dependence structure across observations was specified; no population variance was treated as known or fixed.
commitment_null: H₀: τ = 0, the common site-adjusted treatment effect for the specified population and outcome is zero; the alternative is τ ≠ 0.
commitment_population: Participants in the randomized evaluation at its four sites who were unemployed at random assignment. The target is restricted to this trial population; no broader population was specified.
commitment_outcome: employed_m6: the binary indicator for being employed in the survey week at 6 months, analyzed on its original 0/1 scale without transformation.

commitment_model: For participant i in the selected population, the binary outcome Y_i is modeled with the conditional-mean restriction E[Y_i | T_i, S_i] = α + βT_i + γ_s, where T_i is randomized assignment and S_i is site. commitment_model: For participant i in site s, the modeled conditional mean is E[Y_is | T_i, P_i, s] = α_{s,P_i} + β₀T_i + β₁(T_i×P_i), where T is treatment assignment coded 0/1 and P is parent status coded 0/1. The α terms are unrestricted fixed intercepts for each site-by-parent group. Treatment effects are restricted to be constant across sites within each parent group. The estimand β₁ is the treatment effect among parents minus the treatment effect among nonparents. No parametric observation distribution, known population variance, equal-variance restriction, or cross-participant dependence structure was specified.
commitment_null: H₀: β₁ = 0; the treatment-assignment effects on the conditional mean are equal for parents and nonparents.
commitment_population: Participants enrolled in the randomized evaluation at its four sites, with treatment effects compared by parent status at random assignment (living with at least one child under 18).

commitment_model: For the untransformed binary outcome Y_i = employed_m12, the conditional mean is E[Y_i | T_i, P_i, S_i] = α + β_T T_i + β_P P_i + β_TP(T_i × P_i) + γ_2 1(S_i=2) + γ_3 1(S_i=3) + γ_4 1(S_i=4). This is a linear probability mean model: treatment effects may differ by parent status, with the same effects across sites; there are no treatment-by-site or parent-by-site terms and no other covariates. commitment_null: β_TP = 0, where β_TP is the treatment-assignment effect for participants living with a child under 18 minus the treatment-assignment effect for participants not living with a child under 18, conditional on site in the stated model.
commitment_population: Participants eligible and enrolled in the randomized Pathways to Work evaluation at its four study sites. The estimand is the difference by parent status in the program-assignment effect on 12-month employment, under the model’s common-across-sites effect restriction.
commitment_outcome: Employment in the survey week 12 months after random assignment, employed_m12, used as the original 0/1 indicator without transformation.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None beyond the supplied trial design. No additional filtering by parent status, site, treatment, follow-up, or missingness; parent status enters as a model term for all participants, not as a subgroup restriction. The trial’s enrollment eligibility is part of the supplied design.

commitment_model: For each participant in the selected subgroup, the untransformed binary outcome Y_i has conditional mean E[Y_i | treatment_i, site_i] = α_site_i + τ·treatment_i. Treatment is coded 1 for program assignment and 0 for control; site is represented by fixed indicators for the four evaluation sites. The model imposes one common additive treatment effect across sites, with separate unknown site intercepts. τ is the site-adjusted difference in the conditional probability of food insecurity. commitment_model: For participants with education category 4, the conditional mean model is E[Y_i | T_i, S_i] = alpha + beta*T_i + sum of fixed site indicators for S_i, with one common treatment coefficient beta across sites and no treatment-by-site interaction. Y is observed on its 0/1 scale. No probability distribution for observations or errors, population variance value, homoskedasticity restriction, or explicit dependence structure was specified; site labels 1–4 are conditioned on as fixed indicators, with no random site effects.
commitment_null: H0: beta = 0, where beta is the common site-adjusted treatment difference in the conditional mean of 12-month food insecurity for participants with education category 4.
commitment_population: Participants enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation who had a bachelor's degree or higher at baseline, across evaluation sites 1–4.
commitment_outcome: food_insecure_m12: binary indicator for household food insecurity in the past 30 days at 12-month follow-up, analyzed untransformed on the 0/1 scale.
commitment_sample_restrictions: education == 4 (bachelor's degree or higher). No additional analyst-imposed eligibility filter or complete-case rule; trial enrollment and randomization eligibility come from the supplied design.

commitment_model: Participant-level linear conditional-mean model: E[Y | T,L,S] = β0 + βT T + βL L + βTL(T×L) + site indicators for sites 2–4, with site 1 as reference. T is the observed treatment assignment (0/1); L is 1 for baseline education category 1 (less than high school) and 0 for categories 2–4. The estimand βTL is the difference between the treatment effect for L=1 and the treatment effect for L=0, assumed constant across sites under this model. Covariates and site levels are conditioned on as fixed; no population response or variance parameter was treated as known. No parametric observation distribution, population-variance restriction, or within-site dependence structure was specified.
commitment_null: H0: βTL = 0; equivalently, the treatment effect on 12-month financial security is equal for participants with less than high school education and those with at least a high-school education.
commitment_population: Participants in the four-site Pathways to Work randomized evaluation; the estimand contrasts the treatment effect for participants with baseline education below high school against participants with baseline education of high school or higher. No broader target population was specified.
commitment_outcome: The 12-month financial security index, on its supplied 0–20 scale, without transformation.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None imposed: both education groups and all supplied rows were included, with no analyst-imposed eligibility, subgroup filtering, or complete-case restriction. Baseline education categories 1 versus 2–4 define the model moderator, not an exclusion. This is separate from the trial's enrollment and randomization design and the packet's complete follow-up data.

commitment_model: For Y = food_insecure_m6, the conditional mean is E[Y | T, P, S=s] = α_s + γ_s P + βT + δ(T×P), for site s ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4}; Y remains on its original 0/1 scale. Site-specific baseline means α_s and parent/nonparent gaps γ_s are unrestricted unknown coefficients. The treatment effect is β for nonparents and β+δ for parents, constrained to be common across sites within each parent group; there are no treatment-by-site or treatment-by-parent-by-site terms. The estimand δ is the difference in assignment effects, parents minus nonparents, on the probability scale. No parametric observation distribution, known population parameters, error-variance restriction, or additional dependence structure was specified.
commitment_null: H₀: δ = 0; the treatment effects on six-month food insecurity are equal for parents and nonparents on the probability scale.
commitment_population: Participants enrolled in the randomized trial at its four evaluation sites; the estimand compares assignment effects by baseline parent status within this trial population. No broader target population was specified.
commitment_outcome: food_insecure_m6: an untransformed binary indicator for household food insecurity in the past 30 days, measured six months after random assignment.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None beyond the supplied trial design and enrollment. The interaction model includes both baseline parents and nonparents; no additional eligibility rule, filter, or complete-case restriction was imposed.

commitment_model: Participant-level linear conditional-mean model: E[Y_i | T_i,H_i,S_i] = α + τT_i + β(H_i − H̄) + γT_i(H_i − H̄) + δ₂1(S_i=2) + δ₃1(S_i=3) + δ₄1(S_i=4), where T is assignment, H is baseline household size, H̄ is the analyzed input's arithmetic mean household size, and S is site; site 1 is the reference. commitment_null: γ = 0: the treatment-control difference in the conditional mean outcome does not vary linearly with baseline household size.
commitment_population: Participants enrolled in the randomized evaluation at its four sites; the model conditions on site.
commitment_outcome: Financial-security score at 6 months, on its original 0–20 scale; higher scores indicate greater security.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None imposed by the analyst: no subgroup, filter, or complete-case restriction. The supplied design concerns enrolled adults seeking work or better jobs; the packet states that all participants completed both follow-ups and all variables are observed.

The selected model specifies E[Y_i | T_i, S_i, parent=1] = α + βT_i + γ₂I(S_i=2) + γ₃I(S_i=3) + γ₄I(S_i=4).
