commitment_null: H₀: β = 0, the common site-adjusted treatment effect on the 12-month food-insecurity probability among baseline parents is zero; the selected alternative is β ≠ 0.
commitment_population: Participants in the randomized evaluation who were parents at baseline, pooled across sites 1–4; no broader external target population was specified.
commitment_outcome: The binary indicator food_insecure_m12 (0/1), modeled on its original identity scale; β is a risk difference.
commitment_sample_restrictions: Restrict to parent == 1 at baseline. No additional eligibility, subgroup, or complete-case restriction was imposed.

commitment_model: Linear conditional-mean model for the binary outcome: E[Y | T,F,S=s] = α_s + γ_s F + τT + δ(T×F), where Y is food_insecure_m6, T is treatment, F is female, and S is site. This allows site-specific intercepts and gender differences in baseline outcome, while restricting treatment effects to be constant across the four sites within each gender. The estimand δ is the treatment effect for F=1 minus the treatment effect for F=0. No full observation distribution, normality, homoskedasticity, or known population variance was specified; participant observations are treated as independent. Treatment and gender are coded 0/1 and site is categorical with levels 1–4; no population effects or variances are treated as known.
commitment_null: δ = 0: the treatment effect on food insecurity at 6 months is equal for participants coded female=1 and female=0.
commitment_population: Participants in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at its four study sites, with treatment effects contrasted between participants coded female=1 (women) and female=0 (men); the target is limited to these study sites and groups.
commitment_outcome: Binary food_insecure_m6, coded 1 for reported household food insecurity in the past 30 days and 0 otherwise; analyzed on its original 0/1 scale.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None imposed by the analysis: all supplied observations were included, without a gender-only subgroup or other analyst filter. Trial enrollment and assignment eligibility are features of the supplied design.

commitment_model: Linear conditional-mean model for the 12-month employment indicator: E[Y|T,B,S=s] = α_s + β_T T + β_B B + β_TB(T×B), where T is assignment (0/1), B is baseline employment (0/1), and S denotes site. It includes site-specific intercepts for sites 1–4 and imposes common treatment and treatment-by-baseline-employment effects across sites. The estimand β_TB is the difference between the treatment effect for participants employed at baseline and the treatment effect for participants unemployed at baseline. No parametric observation distribution, population variance values or restrictions, or dependence structure was specified; no population parameters were treated as known.
commitment_null: H₀: β_TB = 0; the treatment effect on 12-month employment is equal across the two baseline-employment groups.
commitment_population: Participants enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at its four sites, considering both baseline-employment groups. No broader external target population was specified.
commitment_outcome: Employment in the survey week at 12 months, represented by the untransformed binary indicator employed_m12 (1 = employed, 0 = not employed).
commitment_sample_restrictions: none

commitment_model: Linear conditional-mean model for 12-month self-rated health: E[Y | T, A, S] = β0 + βT·T + βA·(A − mean age in the analysis sample) + βTA·T·(A − mean age in the analysis sample) + site effects. T is randomized assignment coded 1 for program and 0 for control; S is represented by fixed site indicators for sites 2–4, with site 1 as reference. The treatment effect is constrained to vary linearly with age. Participant observations are treated as independent; no additional clustered dependence structure is specified. No parametric observation distribution, common population variance, or known population variance is assumed. Regression coefficients and site effects are unknown; no population parameter is treated as known.
commitment_null: H0: βTA = 0; the linear change in the treatment effect on 12-month health per year of age is zero.
commitment_population: Participants randomized in the four-site Pathways to Work evaluation; the estimand describes the linear age pattern in the program-assignment effect for this trial population.
commitment_outcome: Self-rated health at 12 months, on its original 1–5 scale (1 = poor, 5 = excellent), with no transformation.
commitment_sample_restrictions: Retain complete cases for site, treatment, age, and health_m12. No analyst-imposed subgroup or other eligibility filter; this complete-case rule is separate from the supplied trial's enrollment and randomization eligibility.

commitment_model: For each participant i in the selected population, let Y_i be the untransformed 12-month financial-security score, T_i ∈ {0,1} the assignment, and S_i ∈ {1,2,3,4} the site. The specified conditional-mean model is E[Y_i | T_i,S_i] = α_{S_i} + τT_i, with unrestricted site-specific intercepts and one treatment effect τ common across sites (no treatment-by-site interaction). No parametric observation distribution, known or restricted population variance, or cross-participant dependence structure was specified.

commitment_population: Participants in the evaluation population at its four sites who had a high school diploma or GED at random assignment; the target contrast is program assignment versus control assignment within this population, conditional on site.

commitment_model: Linear conditional-mean model: E[Y_i | T_i,F_i,S_i,X_i] = β0 + βT T_i + βF F_i + βTF(T_i×F_i) + site fixed effects + common additive baseline-covariate terms. T is randomized assignment; F=1 denotes female and F=0 the comparison group; S includes sites 1–4 with site 1 as reference. X comprises age, parent status, education (categorical, level 1 as reference), household size, baseline employment, baseline earnings, and months unemployed at baseline. The treatment effect varies by F only; site effects and covariate slopes are additive and common across treatment and gender groups. Participant observations are treated as independent, with no other dependence structure specified. No parametric observation distribution, population variance restriction, or known population regression parameter was specified; model coefficients are unknown.
commitment_null: βTF = 0: the conditional mean effect of assignment on 12-month earnings is equal for F=1 and F=0, given site and baseline covariates.
commitment_population: The enrolled-participant population represented by the randomized evaluation across its four sites, comparing participants coded female=1 with participants coded female=0; no broader external population is specified.
commitment_outcome: Raw monthly earnings in dollars at 12 months after random assignment (earnings_m12), including zero earnings where recorded.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None imposed by the analyst: no additional filters, subgroup restriction, or complete-case selection. Trial eligibility comes from the supplied design and is not an added analysis restriction.

commitment_model: For participant i at site s ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4}, the conditional mean of the untransformed 12-month distress score is α_s + γF_i + βT_i + δ(T_iF_i), where treatment T and female indicator F are coded 0/1. This allows the treatment effect to differ by sex, while imposing common sex and treatment effects across sites. The site-specific intercepts and other coefficients are unknown fixed parameters. No parametric observation distribution, known population variance, common-variance restriction, or dependence structure was specified.

commitment_outcome: The Kessler-6 psychological distress score at 12 months, on its supplied 0–24 scale with higher values indicating more distress; no transformation.
commitment_sample_restrictions: None. No analyst-imposed eligibility rule, subgroup filter, or complete-case restriction was applied. The evaluation's enrollment and eligibility conditions are part of the supplied design.

commitment_model: Let Y be six-month self-rated health on its original 1–5 numeric scale, T randomized assignment, S site, and G=1 when baseline months unemployed is at least 12 (G=0 otherwise). Within each group g, the conditional mean is E[Y|T,S=s,G=g]=α_{g,s}+β_gT: site-specific intercepts and a treatment slope common across the four fixed site levels within that group. The selected estimand is δ=β₁−β₀. Participant observations are treated as independent. Outcome distributions and conditional variances are otherwise unspecified; no known variance or equality-of-variances restriction is imposed. commitment_population: Adults enrolled in the four-site Pathways to Work randomized evaluation, comparing assignment effects between the baseline unemployment-duration groups; no broader target population was specified.
commitment_outcome: Six-month self-rated health, recorded from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent), analyzed untransformed as a numeric score.
commitment_sample_restrictions: For the selected contrast, partition participants by baseline months unemployed: at least 12 months versus less than 12 months; both groups are included. No other analyst-imposed eligibility rule, filter, or complete-case restriction was used. Trial enrollment and site eligibility come from the supplied study design.

commitment_model: Within site 2, the conditional mean for participant i is E[Y_i | T_i, X_i, site=2] = α + τT_i + β1 age_i + β2 female_i + β3 parent_i + education-category terms + β4 household_size_i + β5 employed_baseline_i + β6 earnings_baseline_i + β7 months_unemployed_baseline_i. Education is categorical, with level 1 as the reference. Site is fixed at 2. No parametric observation distribution, dependence or clustering structure, known population variance, or equality restriction on population variances was specified; conditional variance is unrestricted. No other population parameters were treated as known or fixed.
commitment_null: H0: τ = 0, the site 2 conditional additive effect of treatment assignment on six-month employment is zero.
commitment_population: Participants enrolled and randomized in the Pathways to Work evaluation at site 2, among the trial's design-eligible adults seeking work or better jobs.

commitment_model: Conditional-mean OLS model: E[Y_i | T_i,D_i,S_i] = α_{S_i} + β_T T_i + β_D D_i + β_{TD}(T_iD_i), where T=1 is program assignment, D=1 means education category 4 (bachelor’s degree or higher), and S is the categorical site indicator for sites 1–4. commitment_outcome: Training enrollment at 12 months, training_m12, coded 0/1 and modeled on its untransformed linear-probability scale.

commitment_model: For participant i, let Y_i be 12-month earnings in dollars, T_i assignment, S_i site, and E_i baseline employment status. commitment_model: Within Site 3, the conditional mean of untransformed six-month earnings is α + τT, where T is assignment coded 0 for control and 1 for program; α and τ are unrestricted. commitment_model: For participant i, on the untransformed binary outcome scale, the conditional mean is E[Y_i | T_i, S_i] = α_{S_i} + βT_i, where S_i is one of the fixed site categories 1–4. commitment_model: For participants in the selected subgroup, the conditional mean is E[Y_i | T_i, S_i] = α + βT_i + γ₂1(S_i=2) + γ₃1(S_i=3) + γ₄1(S_i=4). commitment_model: Individual-level linear conditional-mean model for the binary outcome: E[Y|T,E,S] = α_{S,E} + τ₀T + δ(T×E), where T is randomized assignment coded 0/1, E is baseline employment coded 0/1, and α_{S,E} gives a separate intercept for each of the four fixed sites (1–4) and baseline-employment categories. commitment_model: For Y equal to the binary 0/1 six-month employment indicator, with T the 0/1 treatment assignment, G=1 for education categories 3–4 and G=0 for categories 1–2, and S the site, the selected model restricts only the conditional mean: E[Y|T,G,S]=α+β_T T+β_G G+β_TG(T×G)+δ₂I(S=2)+δ₃I(S=3)+δ₄I(S=4).
